While some models suggest that natural selection is a primary driver that can overcome entropic forces when gene relevance is heterogeneous [5], other research indicates that neutral processes, such as the accumulation of compensatory mutations, can explain high rates of mutation accumulation without requiring the postulate of individual neutral mutations [4].
